result.summary: MapKit JS covers the base map, POI filtering, custom HTML value bubbles and our own overlays, but not all of the cartography on the owner's list. Verified: four map types (Standard, Satellite, Hybrid, Muted Standard); a POI filter that can include or exclude any of 73 categories (Bank, Cafe, Nightlife, Restaurant, School, Park and NationalPark are all present); POIs documented for Standard and Hybrid only; custom DOM annotations; TileOverlay tiles from a URL template or a canvas callback; circle, polygon and polyline overlays. Not documented, so not verified: a 3D view or tilt, terrain or hillshade, national forests, rivers, reservations, route shields on the base map, and any base-map restyling. Costs and limits: $99 per year for the membership; free daily limit per membership of 250,000 map views and 25,000 service calls. Tokens: a console token restricted to carson14dy.github.io can have no expiry; a build job can sign an ES256 JWT with the documented claims (format checked locally with Python, Apple acceptance untested). Legal: the Apple logo and Legal link may not be removed or obscured (license section 2.1 and section 4); Apple map data may not be cached or pre-fetched (section 2.5), so sample or offline builds cannot include it; location features need notice and consent (section F); every doc example loads the library from Apple's CDN, which conflicts with AGENTS rule 4. Versions: 6.1.182 is the newest build on the autoupdate URL (CDN Last-Modified 28 Sep 2026); 5.x (last 5.81.72, 8 May 2026) is not current. Two corrections to the brief: the token page slug is now Creating a Maps token, and /documentation/mapkitjs/mapkit/map is the getter for mapkit.Map (the class page is /documentation/MapKitJS/Map). notes.md was not written, because my instructions bar report or findings .md files; the quotes, URLs and owner steps are in the claims and the source captures are under raw/. Checked on 25 Oct 2026.

claims.claim: Counsel to confirm (a legal reading, not an opinion). Separate hail and address layers are probably not share-alike data. A served Montana extract may be a Derivative Database and carry share-alike on the file itself.
claims.evidence: Reading: a site that draws OSM-derived tiles as its base map and shows its own hail cells and address points as separate layers is most likely a Produced Work (the page the user sees). Share-alike under section 4.4 applies to a Derivative Database that is Publicly Used. A Collective Database is not a Derivative Database under the licence's definition, so if the hail and address datasets stay independent, are drawn over the map, and are not extracted from or joined into the OSM data, share-alike is unlikely to reach them. The line is the combining step: joining hail or address records to OSM features, or publishing one file that holds both, could make that file a Derivative Database. A Montana PMTiles extract is itself an Extraction of OSM data into a new database, so serving it publicly would likely count as Publicly Using a Derivative Database, and share-alike could apply to that file, even though the Protomaps docs call the archive a Produced Work (their label). Attribution applies in every case (O3-2).
